claim: sum_s rank(M_s) over the FORCED slice-space basis of a k-term deficit exceeds j = k-1, so rank(D) > j and the drop-k/add-j lever is refuted for that row. Exact, complete, no search.
derivation: D = sum_s u_s (x) M_s forces span{d_a} <= span{M_s}; at dim span{d_a} = j the fibre space is forced and sum rank(M_s) is basis-independent, so it is the value for EVERY rank-j decomposition of D.
correctsR73: R73 enumerated subspaces U of the first factor as if U were a free variable. It is not: U is determined by the slices once the fibre space is fixed. R73's 3,866,310-subspace sweep is therefore retracted as vacuous — 0 of them were consistent for the reason above, not because the rows are hard.
